bills.title: Protecting kids from deepfakes and exploitative images.
Ban on government social scoring with AI.
Biometric data and license plate readers-regulation.

reading.body:
Wyoming's 2026 legislative activity on AI is narrow: four bills, all finalized by early March, covering deepfakes targeting children, government AI scoring, biometric data, and nonprofit association rules.

The three substantively AI-relevant bills share a single orientation: limiting what governments and unnamed actors can do with data about people. The deepfake bill addresses synthetic imagery of minors. The social scoring bill restricts government use of AI to rank or profile citizens. The biometric and license plate bill regulates automated identity capture. None of the four bills addresses AI development, procurement, or infrastructure.

Because none of these bills touches compute, power, or data center siting, they do not connect to the supply-side constraints this site tracks. They are demand-side rules, concerned with how AI outputs affect individuals rather than with how AI systems are built or powered. The data covers only enacted or finalized legislation through March 2026 and does not reflect any bills introduced or advanced after that date.
